title: A philosophical history of infinitesimals
summary: We explore the issue of providing a foundational framework for Leibnizian infinitesimals in the light of modern standard and nonstandard approaches. We outline a trichotomy of ordinals, cardinals and ringinals as a historiographic tool. A ringinal is a concept of infinite number, arithmetic in nature, different from Cantor's transfinite ordinals and cardinals. The continuum is not necessarily identifiable with R; even if one seeks such an identification, infinitesimals are not ruled out.
